newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends week firm on tighter supply.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends week firm on tighter supply.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended the week firm, after rains tightened supply of raw materials into the market, traders said.
But activity remained flat with most overseas consumers either on holiday or unattracted to current prices, they said.
"It's the end of another dead week," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur. "Next (week) will be worst, with Christmas coming closer."
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted January RSS1 buyer at 317 cents ($1.26) a kg, unchanged from Thursday.
January SMR 20 buyer was quoted two cents up at 308.50.
Traders offered SMR CV at 364 cents, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 319, SMR 10 at 309, SMR 20 at 308 and drum latex at 237.

They said producers were basically holding to current prices because seasonal rains were hampering tapping activities at plantations and reducing the flow of latex and processed rubber into the market.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 240.32 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 12 from 240.31 on Dec 11. The daily indicator price jumped to 240.99 from 240.28.
